clue.text: Prudence unlikely to take these

parts.note: Prudence looks like a woman's name, but read as the quality of caution it is something that avoids gambles and risks

explanation.walkthrough: Prudence with a capital letter poses as a woman; it is the virtue of carefulness, which by nature avoids taking risks.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking risks is taking opportunities that may go wrong, which a careful person avoids.

clue.text: A little heat even in a cold meal

definitions.text: A little heat even in a cold meal

parts.words: A little heat even in a cold meal
parts.note: a small unit of heat energy, found even in food served cold

explanation.walkthrough: The unit of heat is also the measure of food energy, so even a cold meal contains it.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of heat energy, also used to measure the energy value of food.

clue.text: Take turns explaining how to make a net

parts.note: the instruction to alter the letters of nate rearranges them into a net

explanation.surface: Fishermen take turns teaching each other to make nets.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as 'alter nate', the answer is an instruction: rearrange NATE to make A NET.
explanation.definitionFit: To alternate is to do things in turn, one after another.

clue.text: End of Gallic dance (could be a catch in it)

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word Gallic

parts.note: a reel is a Scottish dance

explanation.surface: A French dance finishes, perhaps with a hitch in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The catch is a catch of fish, carried in an angler's basket.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler's wicker basket holds fish that have been caught.

clue.text: An overall attainment

parts.note: overall here means over all others, an achievement of being above everyone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Overall' means total, but read as 'over all' it is being on top of everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Having power or superiority over all others.

clue.text: Second-best suiting?

definitions.meaning: to come off second-best is to be beaten or defeated
suiting is cloth for making suits, such as a smooth woollen yarn fabric

explanation.surface: A suit of clothes that is only the runner-up choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaten in a contest means coming off second-best, and the same word names a firm woollen cloth used for suits.

clue.text: No week-end deity

parts.note: a god who gives his name to a day in the middle of the week, not at its end

explanation.walkthrough: Wednesday is named after this Anglo-Saxon god, and it falls midweek.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-Saxon chief god, equivalent of Odin, after whom Wednesday is named.

clue.text: Rambling talk makes a girl more confused

indicators.note: confused shows the letters of a girl more are jumbled

explanation.surface: Long-winded chatter leaves a young woman more bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, rambling, confused story or procedure.

clue.text: Blake's bright burner

parts.note: William Blake's poem describes a big cat burning bright in the forests of the night

explanation.walkthrough: William Blake's poem opens 'Tyger Tyger, burning bright'.
explanation.definitionFit: The big striped cat of Blake's poem, said to burn bright in the night forests.

clue.text: Their charges may well be fair

definitions.text: Their charges may well be fair

parts.words: Their charges may well be fair
parts.note: charges looks like fees, but here it means the young women in their care, who may be fair or pretty

explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' are not fees but the girls a chaperone guards, and 'fair' means beautiful, not reasonable.
explanation.definitionFit: Older women employed as chaperones for young ladies in Spain and Portugal.

clue.text: The French and the English. meet at the river

parts.note: the French for 'the' is le
the English word for 'the' is simply the

explanation.surface: French and English people gather by a riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lethe is the river of forgetfulness in Greek myth's underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology the dead drank from this underworld river to forget their past lives.

clue.text: Teacher, very eager university leader, is in deep distress

indicators.note: the phrase says one group of letters sits within the other set of letters
distress suggests the letters of deep are troubled and rearranged

parts.note: agog means very eager

indicators.note: leader points to the opening letter of the word university

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic head of a university is struggling badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distress' scrambles the letters of the word deep, and 'is in' places the eager word plus the university's first letter inside that scramble; 'leader' looks like a person, but it only picks a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedagogue is a schoolmaster or instructor, now often a pedantic one.

clue.text: His work is naturally of a pastoral nature

definitions.text: His work is naturally of a pastoral nature

parts.words: His work is naturally of a pastoral nature
parts.note: pastoral suggests countryside and shepherds, but here it means care of souls by a clergyman with a country district

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pastoral' is both rural and to do with a pastor's care; a rural dean is a Church of England priest overseeing a group of parishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric in charge of several country parishes does pastoral work in a countryside setting.

clue.text: He pandered to calf-love .

parts.note: calf-love usually means a youthful crush, but here it is the Israelites' worship of the golden calf in Exodus

explanation.walkthrough: Calf-love looks like adolescent infatuation; it is the idolatry of the golden calf, which Moses' brother made for the people.
explanation.definitionFit: In Exodus, Moses' brother fashioned the golden calf the Israelites worshipped, indulging their idolatry.

clue.text: Trials cut short

parts.note: tests or trials named by a shortened form of their full word, examinations

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the clipped form of a longer word meaning formal tests.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal tests of knowledge are commonly called by this abbreviation of examinations.

clue.text: Where grit may be displayed in flying circles

definitions.text: Where grit may be displayed in flying circles

parts.words: Where grit may be displayed in flying circles
parts.note: grit as courage in flying circles suggests aviators, but it is literal grit whirled about by wind

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grit' looks like pluck among airmen; it is particles of sand swept round in a desert storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert storm whirls sand and grit through the air.

clue.text: Is this lady hermit confined to her bed ?

definitions.text: Is this lady hermit confined to her bed ?

parts.words: Is this lady hermit confined to her bed ?
parts.note: confined to bed suggests illness, but a female recluse was literally walled up in a cell, so shut away

explanation.walkthrough: A woman who lives walled into a cell as a religious recluse is 'confined', though not by illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A female religious recluse living enclosed in a cell, the feminine of anchorite.

clue.text: Suitable type for " big stick diplomacy 3?

definitions.text: Suitable type for " big stick diplomacy 3?

parts.words: Suitable type for " big stick diplomacy 3?
parts.note: big stick diplomacy means threatening foreign policy, but a person who beats with a club literally wields a big stick

explanation.walkthrough: Roosevelt's 'big stick' policy meant backing talks with threat of force; taken literally it suits someone who beats people with a club.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who beats others with a thick stick or club.

clue.text: Swear-word to fill in with

definitions.meaning: a filler word that pads out a sentence or a line of verse

explanation.surface: Bad language used just to pad out what one says.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is called this, and so is any word added only to fill out a sentence or metre.

clue.text: lago's monster was

parts.note: in Othello, Iago warns of jealousy, calling it a monster of a certain colour of eye

explanation.walkthrough: Iago in Shakespeare's Othello calls jealousy 'the green-eyed monster'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jealous people are traditionally described with this colour of eye, from Shakespeare's phrase.

clue.text: They belong to clubs and vice versa

definitions.text: They belong to clubs and vice versa

parts.words: They belong to clubs and vice versa
parts.note: these players are members of clubs, and the clubs (sticks they swing) belong to them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' is both the societies they join and the sticks they own.
explanation.definitionFit: Players of the game with clubs and a small ball are members of clubs and own sets of clubs.

clue.text: Fish about tenpence? Chuck it out !

indicators.note: about means the fish is placed around the other letters

parts.note: an eel is a fish
X is the Roman ten and P is short for pence

explanation.surface: A fish costing ten pence is not worth keeping, so throw it away.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to throw or drive something out.

clue.text: They don't sound such comfortable tenants

definitions.text: They don't sound such comfortable tenants

parts.words: They don't sound such comfortable tenants
parts.note: said out loud, the word for leaseholders resembles 'less easy', so not as comfortable

explanation.walkthrough: The word for tenants under a lease is pronounced like 'less easy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenants holding property under a lease from a landlord.

clue.text: The metal's apparently in the van

definitions.meaning: in the van means at the front, ahead of the rest

explanation.surface: Metal seems to be loaded into the delivery van.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as the metal (lead, rhyming with bed) it is 'lead's'; read as the verb (rhyming with seed) it means is in the vanguard.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the van, short for vanguard, is to be at the front, as one who goes first.

clue.text: She's written articles about it

indicators.note: about means the articles go around the next word

parts.note: an and a are articles in grammar

explanation.surface: A woman has written newspaper pieces on some subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' looks like pieces of writing, but it means the two grammar words used before nouns, which go round the pronoun; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name.

clue.text: Depressing request to an enthusiastic: crowd

definitions.meaning: asking a noisy, eager crowd to cheer not so much

explanation.surface: A dismal plea to supporters who are cheering loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as 'cheer less', the word asks a keen crowd to quieten down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gloomy and dismal lacks any cheer.

clue.text: A loud-mouthed newsmonger

parts.note: a town official who shouted public announcements in the street

explanation.walkthrough: A town crier called out the news to the public.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who calls out public announcements, as a town's news shouter.

clue.text: How wild can a bird become ?

indicators.note: become signals the letters of a bird turning into something else

explanation.surface: How fierce can a bird grow?
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means furious and frenzied, like an animal with rabies.

clue.text: Leader being in trouble, I led a riot

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters of I led a riot are in disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A ringleader confesses to starting a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' is the newspaper's leading article, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader is a newspaper's main opinion article.

clue.text: She appears insular when he's around

definitions.text: She appears insular when he's around

parts.words: She appears insular when he's around
parts.note: a woman next to her partner, joined as groom and wife, seen as insular because a ... surrounds her

explanation.walkthrough: With the groom around her she is 'bride-groom'; the clue's 'insular' plays on her being enclosed by him.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman on her wedding day stands with her groom.

clue.text: It's a bar to freedom of speech

definitions.text: It's a bar to freedom of speech

parts.words: It's a bar to freedom of speech
parts.note: freedom of speech suggests censorship, but this bar is a halting impediment that stops words flowing

explanation.walkthrough: Not censorship: a speech impediment literally stops speech flowing freely.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech impediment with halting repetitions of sounds.

clue.text: Stern guides

parts.note: stern looks like strict, but it is the back of a boat where steering blades sit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' poses as severe; it is the rear of a ship, where its steering blades are fitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships are steered by blades hinged at the stern.
